record.context_brief: survival of antimatter domains with ALP walls
record.original_question: In ALP-based spontaneous baryosynthesis scenarios where high-density antibaryon domains correspond to crossing θ = π and are accompanied by massive domain walls, are domains surrounded by walls with M < M_max sufficiently large to survive in surrounding matter, and what is the subsequent result of the domain-wall evolution?

evidence.quote: In the context of spontaneous baryosynthesis based on ALP physics such high density antibaryon domains can correspond to crossing π. It should be accompanied by massive domain walls at their border.

In such scenario only domains surrounded by walls with M < Mmax can leave the antibaryon domain observable. It puts an open question, whether such domains are sufficiently large to survive in the matter surrounding and what is the result of the domain wall evolution.

artifact.category_tag: ALP domain walls and antimatter domains
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a spontaneous baryosynthesis scenario driven by an axion-like particle (ALP) field θ with periodic potential possessing degenerate minima separated by Δθ = 2π. Suppose that during the cosmological evolution θ traverses the value π in some spatial regions, producing high-density antibaryon domains. At the borders of such domains, massive domain walls form, with surface energy density (wall mass per unit area) M determined by the ALP potential parameters. Let M_max denote the maximal wall tension consistent with the requirement that the antibaryon domain remains observable (i.e. is not collapsed or dissipated by the wall tension before recombination) while not over-closing the universe or contradicting CMB anisotropy bounds.

Assume the antibaryon domains are embedded in an ambient baryonic matter background, so that annihilation occurs at the domain boundary, and the walls evolve dynamically under their tension, friction with the surrounding plasma, and gravity.

(a) Determine, as a function of the ALP model parameters (decay constant f_a, mass m_a, potential height) and the initial domain size R_0, sufficient conditions under which an antibaryon domain bounded by a wall of tension M < M_max survives the surrounding matter (i.e. is not destroyed by annihilation at the boundary or collapsed by the wall) until at least the epoch of recombination.

(b) Describe the long-term result of the domain-wall evolution under these conditions: whether the wall network percolates, collapses into primordial black holes, dissipates into ALP radiation, or leaves observable antibaryon regions, and characterize the final state quantitatively in terms of the model parameters.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether ALP-bounded antibaryon domains with wall tension M < M_max can survive in surrounding baryonic matter, and the eventual fate of the associated domain-wall network, is explicitly stated as an open problem in the BSM cosmology literature. Related works on ALP domain walls and antimatter domains (Khlopov and collaborators) discuss the scenario but do not provide a definitive answer; no published resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Open questions of BSM Cosmology (arXiv listing)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open questions in beyond-Standard-Model cosmology, including the survival of antibaryon domains bounded by ALP domain walls.
status_evidence.claim: The survival of such domains and the result of domain-wall evolution are listed as open problems.
